name: Septimius
summary:
Septimius was a Roman usurper who seized power in the late 3rd century AD. He proclaimed himself Emperor in either 271 or 272 AD, challenging the reign of Aurelian. The short-lived reign of Septimius had significant regional implications for the future of the Roman Empire.

Septimius' ascension to power was a direct result of the political instability and internal conflicts within the empire. His actions were also influenced by the external pressures of the tetrarchy system, which had been established by Emperor Diocletian in an attempt to stabilize the empire's governance.

The legacy of Septimius can be seen in the continued fragmentation of the Roman Empire and the eventual rise of new powers in the region.
